queries.query: the Bhagavad Gita's counsel from Krishna to the grieving Arjuna before battle that the soul cannot be slain and only trades old bodies for new, the way a man changes out of worn garments
queries.note: Chapter II; 'casting off old clothes, puts on others and new ones' paraphrased to worn garments; Krishna/Arjuna are reader-honest (Telang's chunk says 'the Deity'). First draft without the title or battlefield context pulled generic soul-immortality texts (Phaedo, Julian, gnosticism) and missed hinduism entirely.

queries.query: Arjuna begging to see the god's universal form and being overwhelmed by a body containing all the worlds, with countless faces, arms, and terrible jaws
queries.note: Chapter XI theophany; 'many mouths and eyes, with many arms, thighs, and feet' paraphrased to countless faces and arms; 'divine form' rendered as universal form from reader knowledge.

queries.query: the Gita's downward chain where brooding on pleasures breeds clinging, clinging turns to craving, craving flares into anger, and anger wrecks memory and judgment until the person is destroyed
queries.note: Chapter II; 'ponders over objects of sense forms an attachment... from attachment desire... from desire anger... confusion of the memory... loss of reason... utterly ruined' paraphrased to brooding/clinging/craving/wrecked judgment.

queries.query: can taking part in a war ever be a duty rather than a sin
queries.note: Arjuna's crisis on the battlefield — but just-war and nonviolence questions run through several traditions. No target — graded post-hoc.

queries.query: is a life of contemplation superior to a life of action
queries.note: Chapter V's renunciation-versus-pursuit question; monastic and taoist teachings weigh the same choice. No target — graded post-hoc.
